body.statement: The Gaussian-multiplier band in Definition~\ref{def:multiplier-band} has simultaneous fixed-grid coverage \[\Pr\!\left\{\theta_j\in\left[\widehat\theta_j\pm c_{1-\alpha}^\star\widehat\sigma_j/\sqrt K\right]\ \text{for every }1\le j\le J\right\}\to1-\alpha.\] Moreover, with \(\widehat V_R=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\{q^\top(\widehat\Phi_{1,i}-\widehat\Phi_{\theta,i})\}^2\), \[\frac{\sqrt K(\widehat\tau_R-\tau_R)}{\sqrt{\widehat V_R}}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1),\] so the usual two-sided studentized interval has asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\).
body.justification: Joint curve coverage and a scalar grid-RMST interval turn the limit law into clinically interpretable uncertainty statements.
body.gap: Westling et al. (2024, Sections 5.2--5.3) calibrate bands and RMST for directly estimated survival curves; no cited work calibrates the transported spectral counterfactual with estimated donor weights.
body.consumer: TCL investigators can report a familywise-valid untreated survival trajectory and a single treatment-effect interval on the prespecified follow-up grid.

obligation.what_is_open: The multiplier band and studentized grid-RMST proof is complete conditional on Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit}, but that theorem remains open solely through the false frozen first-stage premise.
obligation.obstruction: Without centered joint root-\(K\) asymptotic linearity, neither the sampling maximum nor the scalar RMST statistic has the Gaussian limit used by the conditional multiplier and studentization arguments.
obligation.attempted: Conditional Gaussianity of the multipliers, positive definiteness of the counterfactual covariance block, continuity of the maximum law, quantile convergence, RMST variance positivity, and plug-in variance consistency were derived in full.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(\Omega_\theta\) and \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\) denote the counterfactual \(J\times J\) principal blocks of \(\Omega_\eta\) and \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\).  Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} gives \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\to_P\Omega_\theta\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:nondegenerate-covariance} implies
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\Omega_\theta)\ge v,
 \qquad \sigma_j^2:=(\Omega_\theta)_{jj}\ge v,
 \qquad \widehat\sigma_j\to_P\sigma_j
\]
for every \(j\), because a principal submatrix cannot have a smaller Rayleigh quotient than the full matrix on its coordinate subspace.

Conditionally on the data, the multiplier vector
\[
 Z_K^*=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\xi_i\widehat\Phi_{\theta,i}
\]
is exactly Gaussian with mean zero and covariance \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\).  Therefore its studentized covariance converges in probability to
\(R=\operatorname{diag}(\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}\Omega_\theta
\operatorname{diag}(\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}\).  If \(Z\sim\mathcal N_J(0,R)\), then \(\max_j|Z_j|\) has a continuous distribution: \(R\) is positive definite, so \(Z\) has a density and the boundary of every cube has Lebesgue measure zero.  Continuity of Gaussian probabilities in a positive-definite covariance matrix consequently gives
\[
 c_{1-\alpha}^\star\to_P c_{1-\alpha},
 \qquad
 \Pr\{\max_j|Z_j|\le c_{1-\alpha}\}=1-\alpha.
\]
On the sampling side, Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit}, Slutsky's identity, and the same continuous mapping give
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le J}
 \left|\frac{\sqrt K(\widehat\theta_j-\theta_j)}{\widehat\sigma_j}\right|
 \rightsquigarrow \max_{1\le j\le J}|Z_j|.
\]
Combining the last two displays proves
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\theta_j\in
 [\widehat\theta_j\pm c_{1-\alpha}^\star\widehat\sigma_j/\sqrt K]
 \text{ for all }1\le j\le J\right\}\longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]
The fixedness of \(J\) in Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} is used here; no growing-grid Gaussian approximation is asserted.

For the scalar target, Definition~\ref{def:full-spectral-map} and Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} give
\[
 \sqrt K(\widehat\tau_R-\tau_R)
 =K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K q^\top(\Phi_{1,i}-\Phi_{\theta,i})+o_P(1)
 =K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\tau,i}+o_P(1).
\]
With \(a=(-q^\top,q^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^{2J}\), its variance is
\[
 V_R=E\Phi_{\tau,i}^2=a^\top\Omega_\eta a
 \ge v\|a\|_2^2=2v\|q\|_2^2>0,
\]
where the last inequality uses that the prespecified \(q\) is nonzero.  The same empirical \(L_2\) argument used for \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\) shows
\[
 \widehat V_R=K^{-1}\sum_i
 \{q^\top(\widehat\Phi_{1,i}-\widehat\Phi_{\theta,i})\}^2
 \to_P V_R.
\]
The scalar characteristic-function calculation in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} and division by the consistent positive standard error now yield
\[
 \frac{\sqrt K(\widehat\tau_R-\tau_R)}{\sqrt{\widehat V_R}}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Hence \(\widehat\tau_R\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_R/K}\) has limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).  This is inference for the defined grid functional \(q^\top(s_1-\theta)\); no continuous-time RMST integral is introduced.
